headline: Dry Thursday and Friday, then wetter, windier weather likely early next week.
summary: Western Washington sits between weather systems. A storm offshore moves south Wednesday, bringing only light rain, mostly south of Everett. Later in the week, a ridge of high pressure, a dome of settled, dry air, moves overhead. Farther out, the jet stream, a fast band of high-altitude wind, dips deeply over the Pacific and steers stronger storms toward us early next week. Thursday and Friday look quiet and dry, with temperatures near or slightly below normal. A weak weekend system brings light rain and mountain-pass snow, with little impact. Early next week looks wetter and windier, with more widespread rain, mountain snow, and rivers rising, though no flooding is forecast. Details remain unsettled.
changes: Early discussions focused on cold, foggy mornings and an uncertain weekend rain chance. By afternoon, forecasters added a wetter, windier pattern for early next week, and by evening they described the weekend system as weak with little impact.
